output.brief:
The new CDN is very probably not the cause. Between 12 and 25 October, every Kestria client other than the smart-TV app 5.2 was served by Tessaline and buffered at 0.6–0.7%, the same as before the switch. Only smart-TV app 5.2, released on 9 October, the day of the cutover, stalled, at about 5.9% on every ISP. Devices still on 5.1 were fine. That rules out the CDN, ISP congestion and handball demand as the main cause. Match nights were no worse than other days, and the non-TV clients showed no rise. The likeliest cause is a playback regression in 5.2, probably in how it adapts streaming quality, though I haven't seen the code or release settings.

What to do next:
- Do not send the SLA breach notice, withhold fees or move traffic back. That would punish the wrong party and wouldn't fix the problem.
- Do not mute the alert. It is the one signal still pointing at the real fault.
- Revert 5.2's adaptive-streaming behaviour in Kestria to the 5.1 settings and hold the wider 5.2 rollout until it is fixed.
- Add app version and device breakdowns to the dashboard, at least as an interim query until the Q1 2027 rebuild.
- Hold the free-month offer. The October price rise also fits the cancellation increase, so buffering is not yet shown to be the driver.

I'm fairly confident, about 85%.
